display.purpose: The selected citizen's name on the billboard. Archivo at width 78, uppercase. One per screen.

headline.purpose: The idle billboard's single statement of what the panel is.

wordmark.purpose: The Veritas lockup at width 70, tracked 0.16em. This width step exists for the wordmark alone.

body.purpose: The 14px interface baseline; prose capped at 62-72ch.

body-small.purpose: Secondary text, hints, metadata, small buttons.

label.purpose: Tracked micro-caps at width 105: rail headings, field labels, balance keys, ledger mode.

measure.purpose: Spline Sans Mono, tabular. Citizen IDs, currency, timestamps, counts. Never a label or a sentence.

shadows.name: panel-hairline
shadows.purpose: Module panels at rest: a seam, not a lift.

shadows.name: tile-focus
shadows.purpose: The only heavy shadow in the system, and only under a hovered or focused tile.

shadows.name: rail-lift
shadows.purpose: Declared shadow for a lifted rail band.

shadows.name: tile-edge
shadows.purpose: Hairline inset edge on tile art so a dark plate still has a boundary.

shadows.name: tile-selected
shadows.purpose: Selection ring on the chosen tile: the one pure-white chrome accent.

shadows.name: text-on-art
shadows.purpose: Second legibility guarantee for display text set over a generated plate.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for the focus expansion and rail response.

motion.name: duration-focus
motion.purpose: Tile scale, scrim, caption rise and reveal-row expansion.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Border and background changes on fields and buttons.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.purpose: Honest 1px press travel on every button.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Opacity 1 -> 0.35 on the live rail dot and LIVE badge dot.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Tonal sweep across skeleton tiles while the first page loads.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All authored motion is switched off; also disabled on hover:none pointers and below 560px.

narrative.northStar: The Night Wall of Los Santos
narrative.overview:
Veritas is a catalog of people, read the way its admin reads everything else on the second monitor at 2am: a wall of horizontally scrolling rails of poster tiles on warm asphalt, where the tile under the cursor swells and tells you what it is while the rest of the wall steps back. The ground is deliberately warm near-black (#0D0C0B), not the blue-black the streaming skin defaults to, and the chrome carries no hue at all. Every saturated colour on screen comes from somewhere else: the generated key art. Characters in this product have no artwork, so the artwork is computed from the citizen ID — one deterministic Los Santos sky per record, the same one forever — which makes the image a recognisable property of the data rather than decoration.

The density is operational, not editorial. Controls stand 40px tall because they are clicked mid-session with a game running behind them; the type ramp holds seven fixed steps and admits no in-between sizes; the page never scrolls sideways, only the rails do. Depth is real: an offset-and-blur shadow under the focused tile, a hairline shadow under panels, never a zero-offset halo pretending to be light. Motion is rationed to one authored moment (focus expansion) and it is switched off entirely under prefers-reduced-motion and on touch, where no hover exists to carry it.

The system's discipline is that colour and wording never bluff. Three signals exist and no more, each stated in words before it is stated in hue, because the product's load-bearing distinction — "not on the server" versus "we cannot verify" — must survive a colourblind reader and a monochrome screenshot.
keyCharacteristics: Warm asphalt ground (#0D0C0B), dark-only, chosen from the 2am use scene rather than category habit.
All saturation lives in the generated plates; the chrome is achromatic bone with one pure-white accent.
Exactly three semantic signals, each worded first and hued second.
Archivo run across its width axis (78 / 100 / 105 / 70) instead of across a second typeface.
Spline Sans Mono strictly for measurement: IDs, amounts, timestamps, counts.
2:3 poster tiles on rails; one authored motion moment; everything else still.

rules.name: The Colour Lives in the Picture Rule
rules.body: Saturation belongs to the generated plates and to the three signals. Running prose, record data and every chrome surface stay achromatic. If a new surface needs a colour to be interesting, it needs a plate, not a hue.

rules.name: The Word Before the Hue Rule
rules.body: No state is carried by colour alone. Green is always accompanied by "On the server now" or "Applied live"; amber always by "Status unverified" or "Unverified"; red always by a written direction or failure. A screenshot in greyscale must still read correctly.

rules.name: The Three Lamps Rule
rules.body: There are exactly three signal hues. "Not on the server" is a neutral state and gets bone, never amber — amber means unverified, and collapsing the two would erase the product's core distinction.

rules.name: The Reserved White Rule
rules.body: Pure white appears only where the system says "this one, right now": selection ring, focus ring, focused field border, primary hover. It is never a text or surface colour.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is made by moving Archivo's wdth axis (78 display, 100 interface, 105 micro-caps, 70 wordmark), not by adding a family. A second display face is a system change, not a styling choice.

rules.name: The Mono Is Measurement Rule
rules.body: Spline Sans Mono is permitted only for values that are read digit by digit: citizen IDs, currency, times, counts, server IDs, phone numbers. It never sets a label, a heading, or a sentence.

rules.name: The Seven Steps Rule
rules.body: The ramp has seven declared steps (11 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 22 / 32 / display clamp) and each carries one role. Body copy uses no intermediate value.

rules.name: The Page Never Pans Rule
rules.body: Only rails scroll sideways. If a new surface needs horizontal room, it becomes a rail or a reflowing grid; it never widens the page.

rules.name: The One Gutter Rule
rules.body: Every full-width band uses the same --gutter clamp. Section-specific horizontal padding is drift.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Every surface rests flat on its tone. A cast shadow is a response to hover, focus or selection, never a decoration at rest.

rules.name: The Real Light Rule
rules.body: Shadows have offset and blur. A zero-offset dark halo is not permitted anywhere in this world.

rules.name: The Poster Rule
rules.body: Every citizen tile is 2:3, always. A crop ratio is never varied to fit a layout; the layout changes the tile width instead.

dos: Do put every saturated colour in a generated plate, and keep chrome achromatic bone on warm asphalt (#0D0C0B).
Do state a status in words before you state it in hue; the three signals are green #48E08A live, amber #F5A623 unverified, red #F0503C debit.
Do derive a citizen's key art from their ID through getPlate(), so the same record always shows the same sky.
Do generate a new crop shape when a new aspect is needed, instead of cropping the 200x300 poster.
Do reach for Archivo's width axis (78 / 100 / 105) for emphasis, and keep Spline Sans Mono for measured values only.
Do reserve two lines of caption height on any card in a rail so names share a baseline across the row.
Do keep controls at 40px with honest 1px press travel, and flatten disabled states into the surface.

Do keep the accessibility floor: semantic buttons, labelled controls, pure-white :focus-visible rings, role="status" inline feedback, themed ::selection/caret/scrollbars, and motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do dock new capabilities as another .panel in the module grid, or as another rail in the same grammar.
donts: Don't render "offline" and "unverified" in the same colour or the same words; unknown state stays amber and explicitly unknown.
Don't use pure white for text or surfaces — it belongs to selection, focus and primary hover.
Don't tint running prose or record values with a signal hue; the hue goes on the badge, border, wash or marker beside them.
Don't cast a zero-offset halo or a glow for elevation; shadows in this world have offset and blur.
Don't add a second display typeface or an icon font; the width axis and the authored 24px/1.75 set cover both jobs.
Don't let the page scroll horizontally — only rail tracks do.
Don't add motion beyond the focus expansion, the 2.6s live pulse and the skeleton shimmer; stillness is what makes the one moment read.
Don't replace persistent inline feedback with a toast or an alert(); completed writes stay visible on the record for the session.
Don't design UI implying authentication, permission tiers or an audit trail — none exist.
Don't invent counts, uptime figures or testimonials on any surface.
